question: Who made you?
answer: God made me. I am his creature, called into being by the One who is from everlasting to everlasting, and I belong to him before I belong to anyone else.
kidsAnswer: God made me.
scriptureText: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
commentary: Everything begins here, before any question about what we do or feel. Before a child can earn anything or fail at anything, the first true word over them is that they were made on purpose by a God who was already there. Say it slowly at the table and let the youngest one answer it back.
prayer: Father, thank you that I did not make myself and that I am yours.

question: Is there a God, and how can we know?
answer: Yes, there is one true and living God, and we know him because he has made himself known in all he has made and most fully in his Word and in his Son.
kidsAnswer: Yes, there is one true God, and he shows us who he is.
scriptureText: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the sky above proclaims his handiwork.
commentary: We do not climb up to God by being clever. He comes down to us, in the morning light and in the pages of Scripture, until even a doubting heart has to reckon with him. For the skeptic at your table, the answer is not a clever argument but an invitation to look honestly at what is already speaking.
prayer: God, open our eyes to see you where you have already spoken.

question: What is God?
answer: God is Spirit, infinite, eternal, and unchanging in his being, wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness, and truth.
kidsAnswer: God is the Spirit who never began and never ends.
scriptureText: God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.
commentary: When children ask what God is made of, the honest answer is that he is not made of anything, because nothing made him. He is the one fixed point in a moving world, never older, never tired, never different than he was. That is not a cold fact. It is the ground you stand on when everything else shifts.
prayer: Lord, you do not change, and so we can trust you with everything that does.

question: Is God one, or is God three?
answer: There is one God who exists eternally as three persons, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, each fully God, equal in power and glory, yet one in being.
kidsAnswer: There is one God, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
scriptureText: Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
commentary: No picture fully holds this, and that is fine to admit out loud. The point your family can carry is that God has always been love, because before there was anything to love, the Father loved the Son in the Spirit. We were made to be brought inside that life.
prayer: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, draw us into the love you have always shared.

question: Did God create everything?
answer: Yes, God created all things visible and invisible out of nothing, by the word of his power, and everything he made was very good.
kidsAnswer: Yes, God made everything, and it was good.
scriptureText: And God saw everything that he had made, and behold, it was very good.
commentary: The world is not an accident and it is not a machine. It came from a God who looked at light and water and animals and called them good before a single human had done anything to deserve a good world. Teach your children to receive the morning as a gift and not a given.
prayer: Maker of heaven and earth, thank you for a world you called good.

question: How did God create human beings?
answer: God created human beings, male and female, in his own image, forming us from the dust and breathing into us life, so that we alone among his creatures bear his likeness.
kidsAnswer: God made people, boys and girls, in his own image.
scriptureText: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God he created him, male and female he created them.
commentary: Every person you will ever meet carries something of God in them, which is why no one is ordinary and no one is disposable. This is the deepest answer to the question of who we are, deeper than what we achieve or how we are treated. Look at your children and remember whose image you are raising.
prayer: God, help us see your image in every person, including ourselves.

question: What does it mean to be made in God's image?
answer: To be made in God's image means we were made to know him, to reflect his character, and to rule over and care for his world as those who answer to him.
kidsAnswer: Being God's image means I was made to know him and show what he is like.
scriptureText: And God blessed them. And God said to them, Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it, and have dominion over every living thing.
commentary: Bearing God's image is not a status we keep on a shelf. It is a calling to work, to make, to care, and to represent him in the small kingdom of a home or a classroom. Children grasp this when they see that their kindness or cruelty actually says something about the God they were made to reflect.
prayer: Lord, let our lives show people what you are like.

question: Why did God make you?
answer: God made me to glorify him and to enjoy him forever, finding my deepest life in loving and being loved by the One who made me.
kidsAnswer: God made me to love him and to be happy in him forever.
scriptureText: Everyone who is called by my name, whom I created for my glory, whom I formed and made.
commentary: Glory and joy are not opposites here. We were built so that the surest path to our own gladness runs straight through giving God his due. A family that learns this stops chasing happiness as a thing to grab and starts receiving it as a thing that comes when God is loved.
prayer: God, be our glory and our joy today.

question: Does God control all that happens?
answer: Yes, God rules over all things by his wise and holy will, so that nothing happens by chance, and even hard things are held within the purpose of a good Father.
kidsAnswer: Yes, God is in charge of everything that happens.
scriptureText: In him we have obtained an inheritance, having been predestined according to the purpose of him who works all things according to the counsel of his will.
commentary: This is the truth that holds a family steady when the diagnosis comes or the job is lost. It does not mean every event is good in itself. It means no event has slipped out of the hands of the One who loves us, and that is a different thing entirely from saying God's got this.
prayer: Sovereign Lord, we rest in knowing nothing falls outside your care.

question: Is God good even when life is hard?
answer: Yes, God is always good, for his goodness does not depend on our circumstances, and he works even our suffering toward our good and his glory.
kidsAnswer: Yes, God is always good, even when things are hard.
scriptureText: And we know that for those who love God all things work together for good, for those who are called according to his purpose.
commentary: Do not rush past this one when the family is actually hurting. The verse does not promise that all things are good, only that God is working in all of them. Children learn more about faith from watching parents trust God in a hard week than from any answer memorized in an easy one.
prayer: Father, when we cannot see the good, help us trust the One who is good.

question: What does God require of us?
answer: God requires that we love him with all our heart, soul, mind, and strength, and that we love our neighbor as ourselves.
kidsAnswer: God wants me to love him with all I am and to love other people.
scriptureText: And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength.
commentary: Long before we get to rules, this is what God is after, our whole heart turned toward him and outward toward people. Every command God gives is some version of these two loves. When a child asks what God wants, this is the place to start, not with a list but with love.
prayer: Lord, teach us to love you fully and to love the people near us.

question: How has God spoken to us?
answer: God has spoken to us in his written Word, the Bible, which is breathed out by God, true in all it teaches, and sufficient to make us wise for salvation.
kidsAnswer: God speaks to us in the Bible, his true Word.
scriptureText: All Scripture is breathed out by God and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness.
commentary: The Bible is not a rulebook or a collection of nice sayings. It is God himself speaking, the way a father speaks to children he means to raise. When you open it at the table, you are not reviewing literature. You are listening to a voice that has not gone silent.
prayer: Speak to us, Lord, and give us ears to hear your Word.

question: What is the Bible mainly about?
answer: The Bible is mainly about God's plan to rescue sinners through Jesus Christ, so that from beginning to end its true subject is the saving love of God.
kidsAnswer: The Bible is one big story about Jesus saving us.
scriptureText: You search the Scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life, and it is they that bear witness about me.
commentary: It is easy to read the Bible as a pile of disconnected stories with morals attached. But Jesus said the whole thing points to him. Teach your children to ask of every passage not first what must I do but where is the rescue, because that is the question the book itself is asking.
prayer: Jesus, help us see you on every page of your Word.

part: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
question: How did sin come into the world?
answer: Sin came into the world when our first parents, tempted by the serpent, disobeyed God and ate the fruit he had forbidden, breaking trust with the One who had given them everything.
kidsAnswer: Sin came when the first people disobeyed God.
scriptureText: So when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, she took of its fruit and ate, and she also gave some to her husband.
commentary: The first sin was not a small slip. It was a refusal to trust that God knew best, and that refusal lives in every one of us still. Children understand this better than adults sometimes, because they know exactly what it feels like to want their own way more than they want to obey.
prayer: Father, forgive us for the times we trust ourselves over you.

part: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
question: What is sin?
answer: Sin is any failure to love God and others as we should, whether by doing what God forbids or by failing to do what he commands.
kidsAnswer: Sin is when I do not love God and others the way I should.
scriptureText: Everyone who makes a practice of sinning also practices lawlessness, sin is lawlessness.
commentary: Sin is not only the bad things we do. It is also the good we leave undone and the love we withhold. Naming sin honestly in a home, including the parents naming their own, makes the gospel believable. A child who never hears a parent confess will not believe the parent needs grace either.
prayer: Lord, show us our sin clearly so we can bring it to you.

part: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
question: Did everyone fall into sin?
answer: Yes, in Adam all of us fell, so that every person is born with a sinful nature and apart from grace turns away from God.
kidsAnswer: Yes, everyone is born with sin in their heart.
scriptureText: Sin came into the world through one man, and death through sin, and so death spread to all men because all sinned.
commentary: No one teaches a toddler to be selfish. It comes from inside, which tells us something true and uncomfortable about all of us. This is not a reason for despair but the first honest step toward needing a Savior. We cannot be helped until we admit what is wrong.
prayer: God, we admit the problem is in us, and we need you.

part: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
question: What has sin done to us?
answer: Sin has broken our relationship with God, twisted our desires, brought death into the world, and left us guilty and unable to save ourselves.
kidsAnswer: Sin breaks us and keeps us away from God.
scriptureText: Your iniquities have made a separation between you and your God, and your sins have hidden his face from you.
commentary: Sin is not just a record of wrongs. It is a wound that runs through everything, our relationships, our work, our own hearts. When a family feels the weight of how broken things are, that ache is not faithlessness. It is the right response to a world that is not the way it is supposed to be.
prayer: Lord, we feel how broken things are, and we long for you to heal it.

part: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
question: What is God's law?
answer: God's law is his good and perfect will for human life, summed up in the Ten Commandments, showing us how to love God and our neighbor.
kidsAnswer: God's law shows us how to love him and other people.
scriptureText: And God spoke all these words, saying, I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
commentary: Notice that God reminds his people he rescued them before he gives them a single command. The law is not how we earn his love. It is how rescued people learn to live. Teach your children obedience the same way, as the shape of a life that is already loved.
prayer: God, your law is good, and we want to walk in it because you love us.

part: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
question: What does the law require of us toward God?
answer: The first table of the law requires that we worship God alone, honor his name, keep no idols, and set apart time to rest in him and remember his works.
kidsAnswer: God wants us to worship and love only him.
scriptureText: You shall have no other gods before me.
commentary: An idol is anything we treat as more important than God, and grown-ups have more of them than children do. Money, success, the approval of others, even our own kids can take the throne that belongs to God. Ask each other gently what you would fall apart without, because the honest answer often names your idol.
prayer: Lord, tear down our idols and take your rightful place in us.

part: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
question: What does the law require of us toward others?
answer: The second table of the law requires that we honor our parents, protect life, keep our promises, tell the truth, respect what belongs to others, and refuse to covet.
kidsAnswer: God wants us to be kind, honest, and fair to other people.
scriptureText: Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land that the Lord your God is giving you.
commentary: These commands are not random rules. They protect the people around us, which is what love does. When a child tells the truth even though it costs them, or a parent keeps a promise that has become inconvenient, the household is being shaped by the very heart of God.
prayer: Father, help us love our neighbor in the ordinary choices of today.

part: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
question: Can we keep God's law perfectly?
answer: No, because of our sinful nature we cannot keep God's law perfectly, and even our best efforts fall short of his holiness.
kidsAnswer: No, I cannot keep God's law perfectly on my own.
scriptureText: For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.
commentary: This is the moment the law does its hardest work. It shows us we cannot pull ourselves up to God by trying harder. Every parent who has watched a child promise to be good and fail by lunchtime knows the truth of this in their own bones too.
prayer: Lord, we cannot do it on our own, and we stop pretending we can.

part: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
question: Then why did God give us the law?
answer: God gave the law to show us his holiness, to expose our sin, and to drive us to Christ, who alone kept it perfectly on our behalf.
kidsAnswer: The law shows me my sin and points me to Jesus.
scriptureText: So then, the law was our guardian until Christ came, in order that we might be justified by faith.
commentary: The law is like a mirror that shows the dirt on our face but cannot wash it off. Its job is to send us running to the One who can. When children feel the sting of failing to be good, that is the law doing exactly what God intended, making room for grace.
prayer: God, let the law drive us straight to Jesus and not to despair.

part: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
question: What do our sins deserve?
answer: Our sins deserve God's righteous judgment, for a holy God cannot overlook evil, and the wages of sin is death.
kidsAnswer: Sin is serious, and it brings God's judgment.
scriptureText: For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
commentary: It is tempting to soften this for children, but a God who shrugged at evil would not be good. We want a judge who takes wrong seriously. The very same verse that names the wages of sin turns immediately to a free gift, so do not stop reading at the hard half.
prayer: Holy God, we take our sin seriously because you do.

part: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
question: Is there any hope for sinners like us?
answer: Yes, our only hope is in the mercy of God, who in love sent his Son to save sinners, not because we deserved it but because he is gracious.
kidsAnswer: Yes, God loves sinners and sent Jesus to save us.
scriptureText: The saying is trustworthy and deserving of full acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the foremost.
commentary: After all the bad news, here is the turn the whole catechism has been waiting for. Our hope was never in being good enough. It was always in God being merciful enough. Let the relief of this land on your family before you move on to how it works.
prayer: Merciful God, thank you that our hope rests in you and not in us.

question: Who is Jesus Christ?
answer: Jesus Christ is the eternal Son of God, the second person of the Trinity, who became man to save us, fully God and fully man in one person forever.
kidsAnswer: Jesus is the Son of God who became a man to save us.
scriptureText: And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we have seen his glory, glory as of the only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth.
commentary: Everything in the Christian faith stands or falls on who Jesus is. He is not merely a good teacher or a kind example. He is God who came near enough to be held, and that claim is either the most important thing ever said or the most outrageous. There is no safe middle.
prayer: Lord Jesus, you are God with us, and we worship you.

question: Why did the Son of God become a man?
answer: The Son of God became a man so that he might stand in our place, obeying where we failed and bearing the punishment our sin deserved.
kidsAnswer: Jesus became a man to take our place and save us.
scriptureText: Therefore he had to be made like his brothers in every respect, so that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest in the service of God, to make propitiation for the sins of the people.
commentary: He could not rescue us from a distance. To save people, he had to become one, with skin and hunger and tears like ours. The God who made the stars learned to walk, and he did it for you. That nearness is not a small thing.
prayer: Father, thank you for sending your Son to become one of us.

question: How was Jesus born?
answer: Jesus was conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the virgin Mary, truly human yet without the sin we inherit from Adam.
kidsAnswer: Jesus was born of Mary, with no sin of his own.
scriptureText: The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you, therefore the child to be born will be called holy, the Son of God.
commentary: The Savior had to be one of us, but he could not carry the sin we all carry, or he would need saving too. So he entered the world in a way no one else ever has, born of a woman yet without our broken nature. The manger holds a real baby and a holy mystery at once.
prayer: Lord, thank you that Jesus was both truly human and truly holy.

question: What kind of life did Jesus live?
answer: Jesus lived a life of perfect obedience, loving God and people fully, resisting every temptation, and fulfilling all righteousness on our behalf.
kidsAnswer: Jesus lived a perfect life and never sinned.
scriptureText: For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who in every respect has been tempted as we are, yet without sin.
commentary: Jesus did not only die for us, he also lived for us, keeping the law we could never keep. His whole obedient life counts on our behalf. And because he was tempted as we are, there is no struggle your family faces that he does not understand from the inside.
prayer: Jesus, thank you for living the perfect life we could not live.

question: Why did Jesus have to die?
answer: Jesus had to die because the penalty for sin is death, and in love he took that penalty in our place, satisfying God's justice and opening the way to God.
kidsAnswer: Jesus died to take the punishment for our sin.
scriptureText: For Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring us to God.
commentary: The cross is where the justice and the mercy of God meet without either being cheapened. Sin was punished fully, and sinners were forgiven fully, because the punishment fell on Jesus. This is the center of the whole faith, so linger here longer than anywhere else.
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank you for taking what we deserved so we could be free.

question: What happened on the cross?
answer: On the cross Jesus bore the wrath of God against our sin, was forsaken in our place, and cried out that it is finished, completing the work of our salvation.
kidsAnswer: On the cross Jesus paid for our sin completely.
scriptureText: When Jesus had received the sour wine, he said, It is finished, and he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.
commentary: It is finished are some of the most freeing words ever spoken. The bill is paid in full, with nothing left for us to add. Children who grow up trying to be good enough for God need to hear, again and again, that the work is already done.
prayer: Father, thank you that on the cross the work of salvation was finished.

question: Did Jesus stay dead?
answer: No, on the third day Jesus rose bodily from the grave, conquering death, proving he is the Son of God, and securing the resurrection of all who trust him.
kidsAnswer: No, Jesus rose from the dead and is alive.
scriptureText: But in fact Christ has been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
commentary: The resurrection is not a metaphor or a nice idea about spring. Either a dead man walked out of a tomb or he did not, and everything depends on which. Because he rose, death is no longer the end of the story for anyone who belongs to him, including the people you tuck in at night.
prayer: Risen Lord, thank you that you live and death is defeated.

question: Where is Jesus now?
answer: Jesus has ascended into heaven, where he reigns as Lord over all and intercedes for his people as our great High Priest.
kidsAnswer: Jesus is in heaven, ruling over everything and praying for us.
scriptureText: Consequently, he is able to save to the uttermost those who draw near to God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them.
commentary: Right now, as your family eats dinner, Jesus is alive and praying for you. He is not a figure locked in the past. He is a living Lord who carries your name to the Father. That changes how we pray, because we never pray alone.
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank you that you are praying for us right now.

question: What does it mean that Jesus is Lord?
answer: To say Jesus is Lord means he holds all authority in heaven and on earth, so that he has the right to rule every part of our lives.
kidsAnswer: Jesus is Lord means Jesus is the King of everything.
scriptureText: And Jesus came and said to them, All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.
commentary: Calling Jesus Lord is not a polite religious phrase. It is a surrender. It means he gets a say in our money, our anger, our screens, our marriages. A family that confesses Jesus as Lord at the table is agreeing to let him be Lord in the hallway and the car too.
prayer: Jesus, you are Lord of all, so be Lord of all of us.

question: How are we saved?
answer: We are saved by grace alone, through faith alone, in Christ alone, not by anything we have done but as a free gift from God.
kidsAnswer: We are saved by trusting in Jesus, not by being good enough.
scriptureText: For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing, it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may boast.
commentary: This is the truth that split the church open in history and still sets hearts free today. We do not earn God. We receive him. The hardest thing for a hardworking person to believe is that the most important thing cannot be worked for, only taken as a gift.
prayer: Lord, we stop earning and simply receive what you freely give.

question: What is grace?
answer: Grace is the free and undeserved favor of God, by which he gives sinners what they could never earn and forgives what they could never repay.
kidsAnswer: Grace is God's love that I do not have to earn.
scriptureText: But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
commentary: Grace is not God grading us on a curve. It is God paying a debt we could not pay, while we were still his enemies. The word can become so familiar it loses its shock, so let it land again, that he loved us before we cleaned ourselves up, not after.
prayer: God, thank you for loving us before we ever deserved it.

question: What is faith?
answer: Faith is trusting in Jesus Christ alone for salvation, resting not on our own works but on his finished work, receiving him as Savior and Lord.
kidsAnswer: Faith is trusting Jesus to save me.
scriptureText: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.
commentary: Faith is not pretending to be sure or working up a feeling. It is leaning your whole weight on Jesus the way you lean on a chair you trust to hold you. Children understand trust better than adults, which is why Jesus said we must come to him like them.
prayer: Jesus, we put our whole trust in you and nothing else.

question: What is repentance?
answer: Repentance is a change of heart and direction, in which we turn away from sin and turn toward God, grieving our sin and longing to obey him.
kidsAnswer: Repentance is being sorry for sin and turning back to God.
scriptureText: Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out.
commentary: Repentance is not just feeling bad and then carrying on the same way. It is a turn, a change of road. In a home, repentance looks like a real apology followed by a real change, and children learn it fastest from parents who model both halves rather than just demanding the words.
prayer: Father, give us hearts that turn from sin and turn to you.

question: What is justification?
answer: Justification is God's act of declaring us righteous in his sight, forgiving all our sins and crediting to us the perfect righteousness of Christ, received by faith.
kidsAnswer: Justification means God sees me as forgiven because of Jesus.
scriptureText: Therefore, since we have been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
commentary: Justified means more than forgiven. It means God treats us as if we had lived the perfect life Jesus lived. The slate is not just wiped clean, it is filled with someone else's perfect record. That is why a believer can stand before a holy God without fear.
prayer: God, thank you that in Christ you call us righteous and we are at peace with you.

question: Can anything separate us from God's love in Christ?
answer: No, nothing in all creation can separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus, for those he saves he holds securely to the end.
kidsAnswer: No, nothing can take God's love away from me.
scriptureText: For I am sure that neither death nor life, nor angels nor rulers, nor things present nor things to come, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
commentary: On the hard days, when a child fears they have failed too badly to be loved, this is the verse to return to. The love that saved us is not a love we keep by performing. It keeps us. Nothing on the list, and nothing left off it, can break that grip.
prayer: Lord, thank you that your love holds us and will never let go.

question: What does Jesus give us besides forgiveness?
answer: Besides forgiveness, Jesus gives us himself, making us right with God, adopting us as children, and granting us eternal life that begins even now.
kidsAnswer: Jesus gives us forgiveness and a whole new life with God.
scriptureText: I came that they may have life and have it abundantly.
commentary: Salvation is not only being let off the hook. It is being brought home. Jesus does not save us merely from something but for something, a life with God that is fuller than the one we were living. Forgiveness opens the door, but the gift is God himself.
prayer: Jesus, thank you that you give us not just pardon but yourself.

part: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
question: Who is the Holy Spirit?
answer: The Holy Spirit is the third person of the Trinity, fully God, who applies the work of Christ to us, dwells in believers, and gives us life with God.
kidsAnswer: The Holy Spirit is God living in those who belong to Jesus.
scriptureText: But the Helper, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things and bring to your remembrance all that I have said to you.
commentary: The Spirit is not a force or a feeling but a person, God himself living in his people. He is the one who makes the truths in this catechism more than words to memorize. Pray for him to work, because no amount of teaching changes a heart without him.
prayer: Holy Spirit, come and make these truths alive in us.

part: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
question: What is the new birth?
answer: The new birth, or regeneration, is the work of the Holy Spirit by which he gives spiritual life to those who were dead in sin, making them new creations in Christ.
kidsAnswer: The new birth is when God gives me a new heart that loves him.
scriptureText: Do not marvel that I said to you, You must be born again.
commentary: We cannot give ourselves spiritual life any more than a baby chooses to be born. It is something done to us, a gift from above. This humbles us and comforts us at once, because if God began the work, God will be the one to finish it.
prayer: Lord, give us new hearts that are truly alive to you.

part: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
question: What does it mean to be adopted by God?
answer: To be adopted means God makes us his own children, giving us his name, his care, and a sure place in his family forever.
kidsAnswer: Adopted means God has made me his own child.
scriptureText: And because you are sons, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, Abba, Father.
commentary: God does not merely pardon us as a judge and send us on our way. He brings us into the family as a Father. The word Abba is the tender name a child uses, and God invites us to call him that. For anyone raised without a good father, this is the deepest healing there is.
prayer: Abba, Father, thank you for making us your own children.

part: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
question: What is sanctification?
answer: Sanctification is the lifelong work of the Spirit by which we grow to be more like Jesus, putting sin to death and coming alive to righteousness.
kidsAnswer: Sanctification is God slowly making me more like Jesus.
scriptureText: And I am sure of this, that he who began a good work in you will bring it to completion at the day of Jesus Christ.
commentary: Growth in holiness is slow, and it is not a straight line. Families fail, repent, and grow, and that is the normal shape of the Christian life, not a sign that something has gone wrong. The God who started the work in you and your children has promised to finish it.
prayer: Spirit of God, keep changing us to look more like Jesus.

part: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
question: How does the Spirit change us?
answer: The Spirit changes us by uniting us to Christ, producing his fruit in us, and giving us the desire and power to obey God from the heart.
kidsAnswer: The Spirit helps me love God and grow good fruit in my life.
scriptureText: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control.
commentary: Real change is not us gritting our teeth to be better people. It is fruit, which means it grows from a living root rather than being stapled on from outside. When patience or kindness shows up in a hard moment at home, give thanks, because that is the Spirit at work.
prayer: Holy Spirit, grow your fruit in our home this week.

part: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
question: What is the church?
answer: The church is the whole company of God's people, gathered by the Spirit around Christ, called to worship God, love one another, and make him known to the world.
kidsAnswer: The church is God's family who follow Jesus together.
scriptureText: But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for his own possession, that you may proclaim the excellencies of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.
commentary: The Christian life was never meant to be lived alone. We were saved into a family, not just into a private faith. Showing your children that you need the church, that you cannot follow Jesus well by yourself, may be one of the most lasting things you teach them.
prayer: Father, thank you for your people, and help us love your church.

part: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
question: What is baptism?
answer: Baptism is the sign God gives to mark his people, picturing our union with Christ in his death and resurrection and our cleansing from sin.
kidsAnswer: Baptism is a sign that I belong to Jesus.
scriptureText: We were buried therefore with him by baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too might walk in newness of life.
commentary: The water does not wash away sin, but it pictures the washing only Jesus can do. It is a visible word, a sign you can see and touch, of going down into death with Christ and rising up into new life. Let it remind your family of the cleansing God has promised.
prayer: Lord, thank you for the sign of baptism that points us to Jesus.

part: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
question: What is the Lord's Supper?
answer: The Lord's Supper is the meal Jesus gave his church, where bread and cup point us to his body broken and his blood shed, and we feed on him by faith.
kidsAnswer: The Lord's Supper helps us remember Jesus died for us.
scriptureText: For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes.
commentary: Jesus knew we would forget, so he gave us a meal that preaches to our senses. The bread and cup carry us back to the cross and forward to the day he returns. There is something fitting in how a family that eats together is taught the gospel at a table too.
prayer: Jesus, thank you for the meal that keeps the cross before our eyes.

part: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
question: Why and how should we pray?
answer: We pray because God is our Father who invites us to come to him, and we pray in Jesus name with honest hearts, asking, thanking, confessing, and praising.
kidsAnswer: We pray because God is our Father who loves to hear us.
scriptureText: Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God.
commentary: Prayer is not getting the words right. It is a child talking to a Father who is glad to listen. The simplest prayers at a dinner table teach more about a living God than any lecture, because they show children that he is actually there and actually near.
prayer: Father, thank you that we can come to you about anything, anytime.

part: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
question: What did Jesus teach us to pray?
answer: Jesus taught us the Lord's Prayer, in which we honor God's name, seek his kingdom and will, ask for our daily needs, seek forgiveness, and ask for his deliverance.
kidsAnswer: Jesus taught us to pray, Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name.
scriptureText: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
commentary: When the disciples did not know how to pray, Jesus did not give them a feeling, he gave them words. This prayer is a pattern your family can lean on when your own words run out. Pray it together slowly, and notice that it begins with God's name and his kingdom before it ever gets to our needs.
prayer: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come.

part: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
question: Will Jesus return?
answer: Yes, Jesus will return in glory to judge the living and the dead, to make all things new, and to dwell forever with his people.
kidsAnswer: Yes, Jesus is coming back to make everything right.
scriptureText: This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven.
commentary: History is not running in circles or toward nothing. It is moving toward a day when Jesus returns and sets right everything that is broken. This hope steadies a family in a hard world, because the last word does not belong to cancer or war or death. It belongs to him.
prayer: Come, Lord Jesus, and make all things new.

part: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
question: What is our hope for the life to come?
answer: Our hope is the resurrection of the body and life everlasting, when God will wipe away every tear and his people will see him and be with him forever.
kidsAnswer: Our hope is to live with God forever with no more crying or pain.
scriptureText: He will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death shall be no more, neither shall there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain anymore, for the former things have passed away.
commentary: The story does not end with us floating as spirits on clouds. It ends with bodies raised, tears wiped away by God's own hand, and a world remade. This is the hope you are handing your children, the deepest comfort there is, that the best is not behind us but ahead of us with him.
prayer: Father, hold us in the hope of seeing you and being with you forever.

part: Prayer, the Commandments, and the Christian Life
question: What is prayer?
answer: Prayer is talking with God, who is our Father. We bring him our worship, our thanks, our confession, and our requests, and we trust that he hears us because of Jesus.
kidsAnswer: Prayer is talking with God, who loves to hear us.
scriptureText: Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God.
commentary: Children learn early that prayer is either a performance or a chore. Teach them that it is neither. It is a child climbing into a Father's lap to talk. They do not need fancy words. They need only to know that the One who made the stars bends down to listen to them.
prayer: Father, thank you that we can talk to you about anything, anytime, because you are always listening.

part: Prayer, the Commandments, and the Christian Life
question: How did Jesus teach us to pray?
answer: Jesus gave us the Lord's Prayer, where we hallow God's name, ask for his kingdom and his will, ask for our daily bread, ask forgiveness as we forgive others, and ask to be kept from evil.
kidsAnswer: Jesus taught us the Lord's Prayer.
scriptureText: Pray then like this: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name.
commentary: The Lord's Prayer is the pattern every other prayer can follow. It begins with God, his name, his kingdom, his will, before it ever gets to us, and it teaches a child that prayer is not first about getting what we want but about wanting what God wants. Pray it together until it lives in them.
prayer: Father, teach us to pray the way your Son taught us, with your name and your kingdom first.

part: Prayer, the Commandments, and the Christian Life
question: Why do we call God Father?
answer: Because in Jesus, God has adopted us as his children. We do not come to him as strangers or servants only, but as sons and daughters who are loved, welcomed, and safe.
kidsAnswer: Because God has made us his children through Jesus.
scriptureText: You have received the Spirit of adoption as sons, by whom we cry, Abba, Father.
commentary: Not every child has a good picture of a father, and some carry a wound there. Be gentle. Tell them that whatever an earthly father was or failed to be, there is a Father in heaven who is perfect in love, who never leaves, and who chose them on purpose. For some children this single truth will heal a great deal.
prayer: Father, thank you for adopting us in Jesus, so that we can call you our own.

part: Prayer, the Commandments, and the Christian Life
question: What does God require of us?
answer: God gave us his commandments, summed up in two: to love the Lord our God with all our heart, soul, mind, and strength, and to love our neighbor as ourselves.
kidsAnswer: To love God with everything, and to love others as ourselves.
scriptureText: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength. The second is this: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
commentary: The whole law hangs on love. Teach your children that God's commands are not a list of cold rules but a description of what love looks like, and that when we keep them we are living the way we were made to live. The commandments are the shape of a good life, not the enemy of it.
prayer: Lord, give us hearts that love you above all and love our neighbors as ourselves.

part: Prayer, the Commandments, and the Christian Life
question: What are the Ten Commandments?
answer: God's good law, given at Sinai: to have no other gods, make no idols, honor his name, keep the Sabbath, honor parents, and not to murder, commit adultery, steal, lie, or covet.
kidsAnswer: God's ten good rules that teach us to love him and love others.
scriptureText: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt. You shall have no other gods before me.
commentary: Notice that God rescued his people first and gave the commandments second. The law was never how Israel earned his love. It was how a rescued people learned to live free. Teach your children obedience the same way, as the grateful response of the already loved, never as the price of being loved.
prayer: Lord, thank you for rescuing us first, and teaching us to live well second.

part: Prayer, the Commandments, and the Christian Life
question: Can we keep God's law perfectly?
answer: No. We all break God's law in what we do and fail to do, and the law shows us our sin and our need for a Savior. Only Jesus kept it perfectly, in our place.
kidsAnswer: No, only Jesus kept it perfectly, for us.
scriptureText: For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.
commentary: The law is a mirror before it is a map. It shows children their real need before it shows them the way to live, and that is a mercy, because a child who thinks they can be good enough on their own has not yet understood the gospel. Let the law drive them to Jesus, who kept it for them.
prayer: Jesus, thank you for keeping God's law perfectly in our place, when we could not.

part: Prayer, the Commandments, and the Christian Life
question: What should we do when we sin?
answer: We confess our sin to God, who is faithful and just to forgive us because of Jesus, and we turn from it. We do not hide or pretend, because there is no sin too big for the cross.
kidsAnswer: We tell God we are sorry, and he forgives us because of Jesus.
scriptureText: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
commentary: The most important thing you can teach a child about sin is that the way home is always open. A child who learns to run toward God when they fail, rather than away from him, has learned the secret of the Christian life. Make confession in your home safe, quick, and followed by warmth, the way the Father met the prodigal.
prayer: Father, thank you that when we confess our sin, you always forgive us and welcome us home.

part: Prayer, the Commandments, and the Christian Life
question: Why do we gather with the church?
answer: Because God saves us into a family, not alone. With the church we worship God, hear his Word, share the Lord's Supper, and help one another follow Jesus all the way home.
kidsAnswer: Because God makes us part of his family, the church.
scriptureText: Let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works, not neglecting to meet together.
commentary: Children should grow up knowing that following Jesus is a team sport, never a solo one. The church is not an optional add-on to private faith but the family God adopts us into. Help them belong to it, love it, and serve in it, so that the body of Christ becomes part of how they know they are not alone.
prayer: Father, thank you for the church, your family, where we help one another follow you.

part: Prayer, the Commandments, and the Christian Life
question: What is baptism?
answer: Baptism is a sign of belonging to God. The water points to being washed clean by Jesus and joined to his death and resurrection, marking us as members of God's covenant family.
kidsAnswer: Baptism is a sign that we belong to God and are washed clean by Jesus.
scriptureText: Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
commentary: Use baptism as a teaching moment whenever your church practices it. Let your children watch the water and ask what it means, and tell them it is God putting a visible sign on an invisible promise, that those who trust Jesus are washed, claimed, and welcomed into his family forever.
prayer: Father, thank you for the sign of baptism, that those who trust you are washed and claimed as your own.

part: Prayer, the Commandments, and the Christian Life
question: What is the Lord's Supper?
answer: The Lord's Supper is a meal Jesus gave us, where bread and cup point to his body broken and his blood shed for us. We receive it together to remember him and feed on him by faith.
kidsAnswer: It is the meal where we remember Jesus gave his body and blood for us.
scriptureText: This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.
commentary: The table is a sermon a child can see and taste. Even before they take it, let them watch and ask, and tell them that the bread and the cup are how Jesus reminds his family, again and again, that he gave himself for them. The gospel is something we eat, not only something we hear.
prayer: Jesus, thank you for the Supper, where we remember that you gave yourself for us.

part: Prayer, the Commandments, and the Christian Life
question: How does the Holy Spirit change us?
answer: The Spirit lives in every believer, giving us new life and slowly growing his fruit in us: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.
kidsAnswer: The Holy Spirit lives in us and grows his good fruit in our lives.
scriptureText: The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control.
commentary: Children try hard to be good and fail, the same as adults. Teach them that becoming like Jesus is not finally something they manufacture but something the Spirit grows, like fruit on a branch that stays connected to the vine. Their job is to stay close to Jesus. The growing is his work, and it is slow, and it is sure.
prayer: Holy Spirit, live in us and grow your good fruit in our lives, day by day.

part: Prayer, the Commandments, and the Christian Life
question: Why did God make you?
answer: God made me to know him, love him, enjoy him, and live for his glory forever. My deepest happiness and his glory are not two things but one, found in him.
kidsAnswer: God made me to know him, love him, and be happy in him forever.
scriptureText: Everyone who is called by my name, whom I created for my glory, whom I formed and made.
commentary: End where the catechism began, with the child and their Maker. The whole story you have been teaching comes down to this, that they were made by God and for God, and that they will never be at rest until they are at rest in him. This is the deepest thing your children can know about themselves, and it is worth a lifetime of saying.
prayer: Father, you made us for yourself. Help us know you, love you, and be happy in you forever.

question: If God is good, why is there suffering and evil?
answer: Suffering and evil are real, and God did not make a broken world. The world went wrong when people turned away from God, and that ruin spread into everything. God is good, and rather than leaving us in the mess, he entered it himself in Jesus to carry our suffering and one day to end it forever.
kidsAnswer: God is good, and one day he will end all suffering for good.
scriptureText: He will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death shall be no more, neither shall there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain anymore.
commentary: Do not rush to defend God when a child is genuinely hurting. The Bible never treats suffering as a small thing or pretends it is good. The deepest answer is not an explanation but a person, a God who did not stay at a safe distance but came down and suffered with us and for us. Let your child know that God hates the pain even more than they do, and that he has promised to undo it.
prayer: Father, you hate suffering more than we do, and we trust you to end it.

question: Is the Bible really true?
answer: Yes, the Bible is true, given by God through real people over many centuries, written down, copied carefully, and held up to testing for thousands of years. More than a collection of facts, it tells the one true story of how God made us, how we went wrong, and how Jesus came to save us, and that story has the ring of truth that no one could have invented.
kidsAnswer: Yes, the Bible is God speaking to us, and it is true.
scriptureText: Sanctify them in the truth, your word is truth.
commentary: A child who asks this is not being rebellious. They are growing up, and honest questions deserve honest answers. You do not need to pretend you can prove every line. You can show them that the Bible has been tested harder than any book in history and still stands, that it tells the truth about the human heart, and that it points to a Jesus too real to be made up. Welcome the question. A faith that cannot be questioned cannot be trusted.
prayer: Lord, thank you that your word is true, and help us trust it.

question: How do we know God is real if we cannot see him?
answer: We cannot see God with our eyes because he is Spirit, but we know real things we cannot see all the time, like love, or the wind, or our own thoughts. God has made himself known in the world he made, in his written word, and most clearly in Jesus, who is God we could see and touch and hear.
kidsAnswer: We cannot see God, but he has shown us who he is in Jesus.
scriptureText: No one has ever seen God, the only God, who is at the Father's side, he has made him known.
commentary: Children think in pictures, so the unseen can feel unreal to them. Help them notice all the real things they cannot see, starting with the love you have for them. Then point them to Jesus, who is the answer to this very question. When people wanted to see God, God came as a baby, grew up, and walked among us. We do not know God by squinting harder. We know him because he came close.
prayer: God, even though we cannot see you, help us know you are near.

question: What about people who never heard about Jesus?
answer: This is a question we can trust to God, who is more just and more merciful than we are. The Bible teaches that no one is saved apart from Jesus, but it also tells us that the Judge of all the earth will do what is right, and that he leaves no one without some witness to himself. We can rest in his goodness even where we do not have every answer.
kidsAnswer: We do not know everything, but we know God is always fair and kind.
scriptureText: Shall not the Judge of all the earth do what is just?
commentary: It is fine, even good, to admit you do not fully know. What you can give your child is confidence in God's character. He is never unfair, never cruel, never careless with a single person. The same question can also stir a family toward mission, because if people need to hear, then someone must go and tell. Hold the mystery and the urgency together, and do not resolve too quickly what God has left partly hidden.
prayer: Father, we trust you to be perfectly fair and kind with every person.

question: Is Jesus really the only way to God?
answer: Yes, Jesus is the only way to God, not because God is narrow but because the problem of our sin is so deep that only God himself could fix it, and he did, in Jesus. Jesus is not one good teacher among many. He is the one who actually died and rose to open the door home, and that door is open wide to everyone who comes.
kidsAnswer: Yes, Jesus is the only way home to God, and the door is open to all.
scriptureText: Jesus said to him, I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
commentary: This sounds harsh to modern ears, so explain it with care. Jesus being the only way is not God shutting people out but God doing for us the one thing we could never do for ourselves. A drowning person does not complain that there is only one rope. The exclusiveness of Jesus is matched by the openness of his invitation, for he turns no one away who comes to him.
prayer: Jesus, thank you for being the way home, and for welcoming all who come.

question: What happens when we die?
answer: When we die our bodies stop, but we do not stop existing. Those who trust Jesus go to be with him, which is a joy beyond anything here, and they wait for the day he raises their bodies new and whole. Death is real and sad, but for those who belong to Jesus it is not the end. It is a door into being with him.
kidsAnswer: When those who love Jesus die, they go to be with him.
scriptureText: My desire is to depart and be with Christ, for that is far better.
commentary: Children often ask this after a loss, so let your tone be gentle and your tears welcome. Do not pretend death does not hurt, because it does, and Jesus himself wept at a grave. But tell them the truth that takes the terror out of it, that for the friend of Jesus, death is being carried home into the arms of the One who made them. The body sleeps for a while, and then it will rise.
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank you that death cannot separate us from you.

question: Did God make dinosaurs, and how does science fit with the Bible?
answer: Yes, God made everything, including dinosaurs, and all that is true in science is simply discovering more of the world he made. The Bible tells us who made the world and why, and science studies how the world works. They are answering different questions, and a child can love both, marveling at God as the Maker behind it all.
kidsAnswer: Yes, God made everything, even dinosaurs, and science studies his world.
scriptureText: For by him all things were created, in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, all things were created through him and for him.
commentary: Do not make your child choose between loving God and loving science, because that is a false choice that drives many away later. Faithful Christians hold different views on the timing and method of creation, and that freedom is fine. What every Christian shares is the conviction that God made it all on purpose. Let dinosaurs and galaxies be doorways to worship, not walls between your child and faith.
prayer: Maker of all things, thank you for a world so wonderful to explore.

question: Why does God sometimes say no to our prayers?
answer: God always hears our prayers, and like a good father he answers in the way that is truly best, which is sometimes yes, sometimes wait, and sometimes no. A loving parent does not give a child everything they ask for, because love sees further than wanting does. God's no is never a sign he stopped caring. It is the answer of a Father who knows more than we do.
kidsAnswer: God answers every prayer in the way that is best, even when it is no.
scriptureText: But he said to me, My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.
commentary: Children feel a no from God deeply, especially when they prayed for something good. Help them see that you, as their parent, also say no to things they want, not because you are cruel but because you love them and see further. God is the perfect Father doing the same. Teach them that even Jesus prayed for a hard thing to pass and the Father said no, and that no led to our rescue.
prayer: Father, help us trust your answer even when it is not the one we wanted.

question: What about other religions?
answer: People in every place have searched for God, and many religions hold pieces of truth and real longing. Yet the Bible tells us that we do not finally find God by climbing up to him through our own efforts. He came down to us in Jesus. We can respect and love people of every faith while still believing that Jesus is the one God sent to save us all.
kidsAnswer: Other people search for God, and we believe Jesus is the one God sent.
scriptureText: And there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved.
commentary: Teach your children to hold two things at once, deep respect for people who believe differently and deep conviction about Jesus. Most other faiths tell people what to do to reach God. The gospel tells what God has already done to reach us. That is the difference worth naming gently. Train your children to love their neighbors of other faiths warmly, never to look down on them, and to be ready to tell them about Jesus.
prayer: Lord, help us love people of every faith and point them to Jesus.

question: Will God ever stop loving me if I am bad?
answer: No, God will never stop loving you. His love for his children does not rise when you are good or fall when you are bad, because it was never based on you in the first place. It is based on Jesus, who loved you to the cross. You can disappoint God and grieve him, but you cannot make him stop loving you, ever.
kidsAnswer: No, God will never, ever stop loving you.
scriptureText: For I am sure that neither death nor life, nor things present nor things to come, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
commentary: This may be the most important answer in this whole section, so say it again and again. A child who fears that their badness can cancel God's love will hide from him exactly when they most need to run to him. Tell them the love of God is not a wage they earn but a gift that holds them. When they fail, the right move is to run toward God, not away, because his arms stay open.
prayer: Father, thank you that nothing we do can make you stop loving us.

question: Why do bad things happen to good people?
answer: The Bible tells us honestly that hard things happen to people who do not deserve them, and it does not pretend otherwise. We live in a world broken by sin, where pain falls on everyone, the kind and the cruel alike. Yet God promises to be with his people in their suffering and to work even hard things toward good for those who love him.
kidsAnswer: Hard things happen in a broken world, and God is with us in them.
scriptureText: And we know that for those who love God all things work together for good, for those who are called according to his purpose.
commentary: Resist easy answers here, because this question often comes when a family is actually hurting. The Bible has a whole book, Job, that refuses to give a tidy reason for one man's suffering and instead points him to the greatness of God. The most truthful thing you can tell a child is that we do not always know why, but we do know who is with us, and that the worst thing is never the last thing for those who belong to him.
prayer: Lord, when we cannot understand the why, hold us close in the hurt.

question: How can God be three and one at the same time?
answer: We call this the Trinity, that God is one God who lives forever as three persons, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. This is not a riddle to solve but a wonder to receive. It means God has always been love, because before he made anything to love, the Father loved the Son in the Spirit. We were made to be brought inside that love.
kidsAnswer: There is one God who is the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
scriptureText: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ and the love of God and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.
commentary: Do not try to make the Trinity simple, because every neat illustration eventually says something untrue. It is fine to tell your child that this is bigger than our minds, and that a God we could fully fit in our heads would not be much of a God. What they can carry is the wonder of it, that God did not become loving when he made us. He has been love forever, three persons in perfect joy, and he made us to share in it.
prayer: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, draw us into the love you have always known.
